newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU expects more pro-EU stand from Blair.
newsitem.headline: German CDU expects more pro-EU stand from Blair.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government should be more open to majority voting in the European Union on some economic issues and ready to grant greater powers to the European Parliament, a German foreign policy expert said on Wednesday.

Karl Lamers, foreign policy spokesman for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said new British Prime Minister Tony Blair was fundamentally pro-European and would be more flexible towards the EU than predecessor John Major.

"There are opponents of Europe in the Labour party, too, but Labour's majority is so huge that Tony Blair does not have to take these critics into consideration," Lamers told Berlin's InfoRadio station.
"The absolute paralysis of (Major's) Tory government was not in Britain's best interests," he said.
Lamers said he expected Britain, which until now had firmly opposed majority voting on many key EU policies, to give up its veto on some economic issues.

He did not elaborate. Doug Henderson, Britain's new minister for Europe, told EU colleagues on Monday London would end its opt-out from the EU's Social chapter and support an employment chapter in the new EU treaty to be adopted in mid-June in Amsterdam.
Lamers said he also expected Britain to agree to more powers for the European Parliament.
But the Labour government would still stress Britain's sovereignty in some areas, such as border controls, he added.
